story:
Emily’s POV

Tonight. I have to leave tonight.

I sat down on my stone bed, thinking about my life so far. Nyx has been holding on for too long. I can't let her go through this anymore.

I used to be almost everyone's favorite in the pack until Mom and Dad passed. I don't know what came over Ryan's mom and dad. It felt like they were waiting for a chance to push me aside. They used to be very nice until they were not.

People who were not in the pack before that incident did not know I was the daughter of the last Alpha and Luna.

Everybody in the wolf world thought I was dead; at least, that's what I heard.

I can't let him break what strength I have left. I won't let him keep me trapped any longer. I have to come up with a plan; I don't care if I die running; I have to leave this cruel and cold-hearted pack before I am humiliated.

I have to eat this afternoon; I'll need the energy if I'm going to be running. He'll surely send others after me, so I have to be in my wolf form.

"Nyx, you there?" I mindlinked her, and she whimpered in response in my head. "I'll need you tonight, girl. I'll need you if I'm ever going to make it out alive. I can't let him do this to me, to us. We have to find a way to break free from this life. We waited because we thought we might find love, but it's over now, Nyx. We need to run," I said pleadingly to her.

"I don't know if I can do it for us, Emily. What if we get killed on sight because of my fur color? What if he catches up to us? What if we don't make it alive? I'm so weak, and I've only ever shifted once. I don't want to let you down, Emily," Nyx said weakly in my head, and fresh tears ran down my cheeks. We don't deserve any of this.

"Nyx, we need to try, girl. There's a full moon out tonight. I heard we get stronger when there's a full moon. Maybe that will give us the strength to propel forward, but we can't stay here tonight. We might find help in another pack. Anything but here, Nyx," I said to her.

"You're right. We've been taking this for too long. It's time we break free and start over. We run tonight," Nyx said in my head with newfound determination.

Her words made me see rays of hope. I stood up and made my way to the pack kitchen to see if there was any food I could make do with until evening. I needed to eat to at least get enough energy to run.

I went to the kitchen, and kitchen workers were hurrying around preparing a feast for my sister Beatrice and Ryan's coronation. I was disappointed and was about to leave when I spotted Jane. Jane is an elderly woman who used to be our head cook. She's the only one in the pack who doesn't treat me like I'm beneath her. She avoided showing kindness to me in public—people would notice.

She saw me as I was about to leave, too, and came to meet me in the hallway. She hugged me with tears in her eyes, and I hugged her back, too. She has always been like a grandmother to me.

She led me into a quiet hallway corner and burst into tears as she took in my condition. She's not been to the pack in a while; I guess she quit her job, but why was she back tonight? I saw her mouth moving and tried to listen to her over her thoughts.

"...heard he rejected you and chose Beatrice anyway. I'm so sorry, Emily. No one deserves to be treated like that by their mate," she whispered with tears running down her cheeks, and I hugged her again.

"You look malnourished, child. Do they ever feed you? I'm sorry I left without telling you. I had to go see family in another pack. It's been a while since I could visit," she told me while looking me over. My stomach chose that moment to grumble again. I looked down in embarrassment.

"Have you had anything to eat today, child?"

I shook my head negatively, and she told me she'd be back for me. As she left, I tried to make myself small and invisible to anyone passing. I need to stay calm today; I must preserve my energy to escape safely.

Jane soon came back with a paper bag in her hand. She gave it to me and hugged me tightly after telling me to live well. It was almost like she knew I was going away. I thanked her and left for the basement again.

I could not eat a lot. It was almost like my body was used to not being fed and rejected the food. I sighed as I kept the paper bag. I had to hide it carefully—if someone found it, it might cause problems.

I was waiting for night to fall and the coronation to start while praying to the moon goddess to give me the energy and luck to escape this place that has brought me nothing but suffering.

I shook in my seat when I heard footsteps coming down the basement. I looked up and saw one of the pack guards and slightly relaxed. They're not as bad as the high-ranking wolves.

"It's time for the coronation, and Alpha Ryan requires you to be near the ballroom," his deep voice boomed, making me jump in my seat, and I nodded my head. He turned to leave, and I followed after him. I don't want to incur wrath on myself.

I followed him to where the coronation was taking place. It looked beautiful and magnificent. Beautiful flowers were used to create an arch in the doorway and were also scattered across the room. People dressed in white. Women in elegant gowns and men in fitting suits were scattered around the room, chatting.

I stood out in my dirty attire and unkempt appearance. I knew Ryan brought me there to humiliate me and show me that I'd never be his Luna because I was below him. People glanced at me curiously, some whispering under their breath as I passed, but I kept my head down the whole time. I stood to the side in the ballroom and made myself small.

The chatters in the room suddenly quieted down, and I looked up to see Ryan in a black suit that was perfectly tailored to suit him and my sister in a blood-red gown with a thigh-high slit that accentuated all of her curves.

Beatrice looked so good with her hair in waves that she let it down to frame her beautiful face. Her make-up looked minimal, and I could not even deny the fact that she looked stunning. Together, they looked amazing, and Nyx whimpered inside me, heartbroken at the sight of her mate with another.

They made their way to the stage, and people started clapping, focusing all of their attention on them. Ryan glanced my way and gave a cold, knowing smirk. That look sent a chill down my spine because I knew what awaited me if I didn't escape before the coronation ended.

Everybody focused their attention on their future rulers, and I took that opportunity to sneak out of the ballroom and out of the pack house. The moon was high up in the sky and shone brightly, almost like the Moon Goddess was making way for me.

I made my way to the end of the pack, avoiding patrols and guards. Security is not as tight at the pack boundary, so I thanked the Moon Goddess. Right before I morphed into my wolf, I said the words I should have said since the moment I knew he wasn't going to choose me.

Using my original title, I said those words.

"I, Emily Leyly, daughter of the last Alpha and Luna of the Gray Moon Pack, accept the rejection of Ryan Whitmoor, son of the Betas of this pack, as his mate and chosen one," I said and felt a surge of power through me at the same time I heard a wolf howling in pain in the distance.

Nyx took over my body, and I was a pure white wolf. I felt a new burst of energy coursing through my veins. Then I ran. I ran with everything in me and never looked back.

stories.cover:
Ryan had just claimed my pregnant sister as his Luna in front of the entire pack. I couldn't watch
anymore.

I slipped to the back of the hall, where everyone celebrated a bright future while mine fell apart. I
had lost my mate. I was alone.

I sank into an empty chair, trying to steady my breathing and stop the tears. I didn't care where I was.
I just wanted to disappear.

But the moment I slumped into the seat, a sudden realization hit me.

I had sat next to someone huge. His muscular build barely fit in the chair, and I felt a sudden warmth
where our legs touched. His arms were covered in dark tattoos, and his presence felt magnetic and
intense. He was sitting far from the stage, deliberately hidden from the crowd.

I glanced up in shock and froze.

His dark eyes locked onto mine. There was something powerful and commanding in his gaze. I felt warmth
rush through me, and my inner wolf responded in a way she had never felt before—not even with Ryan.

Startled, I sat up straighter. I needed to leave. Now. Before Ryan or the guards saw me sitting next to
a guest.

But before I could even stand, the stranger reached out, his fingers brushing lightly over my wrist.

“Wait,” he said softly.

His voice was a low, rumbling baritone that vibrated right through my bones. Something in me wanted to
listen. To my surprise, my wolf didn't want to pull away either.

Suddenly, the roaring music faded, and nearly everyone in the grand hall turned to look straight at us,
their eyes wide with shock.

"Why... why are they staring at us?" I whispered, my voice trembling as panic seized my throat.

The stranger studied my tear-streaked face, my disheveled dress, and my messy hair before a smirk played
on his lips.

“Because you’re the first person to ever sit by me willingly.”

And then, a sudden realization crashed into me.

The tattoos, his powerful presence, and the empty royal seat next to Alpha King Garrett at the front of
the room told me exactly who he was. I had sat beside the Alpha King’s son. His dark eyes sharpened as
he noticed my panic.

"Interesting," he murmured.

Over his shoulder, I caught Ryan's glare. Beta Thomas was already making his way toward me. I pulled my
hand back before the Alpha King’s son could say another word.

I bolted.

“Hey! Wait!” I heard someone say.

I didn’t look back. I couldn't.
